name: ssd1306
description: SSD1306 OLED display driver via I²C. Supports 128x64 and 128x32 panels. Inherits from framebuf.FrameBuffer — supports text, lines, rectangles, pixels. Sub-package ssd1306_cn adds Chinese character rendering.

constructor_params.name: i2c
constructor_params.description: Initialized I2C object (user creates with machine.I2C)

constructor_params.name: external_vcc
constructor_params.description: True if display powered externally (affects charge pump config)

methods.name: show
methods.description: Flush frame buffer to display (REQUIRED after any draw call)

methods.name: text
methods.description: Draw text at (x,y). Uses built-in 8x8 font for ASCII.

sub_packages.ssd1306_cn: Chinese character rendering extension (separate module in lib/ssd1306_cn/)

example:
from machine import I2C, Pin
from ssd1306 import SSD1306

i2c = I2C(1, scl=Pin(22), sda=Pin(21), freq=115200)
screen = SSD1306(128, 64, i2c)
screen.text('Hello, World!', 0, 0, 1)
screen.show()
test_method: SSD1306.test()    # interactive test (prompts for SCL/SDA pins)
esp32_notes: All draw methods write to frame buffer — must call show() to display
Default I²C frequency 115200 — works for most displays. Try 400000 for faster refresh.
Built-in 8x8 font only supports ASCII (32-126). For Chinese, use ssd1306_cn sub-package.
I2C(1, ...) uses GPIO21/22. I2C(0, ...) uses GPIO1/3 (UART — avoid).
hardware_notes: Most SSD1306 modules work at 3.3V. Some 5V modules include on-board regulator.
SCL/SDA need 4.7kΩ pull-up resistors (most modules include them)
Run I2C.scan() first if uncertain about address
differences_from_standard_mp: SSD1306 wraps framebuf.FrameBuffer — adds show(), poweron/off(), contrast(), invert() methods
Standard framebuf has no display-flush concept. show() is the NovaMP addition.
